Visitors wearing badges are walking in both directions, and some are stopping to talk at the booths. In the middle of the aisle, a floor map stands on a stand with a 'You are here' marker. Near the entrance, a registration desk has a short line. At the back, a stage has a small group watching a demonstration. For newcomers, the best thing is to look at the floor map first and then plan a route.

This is the central quad of a university at lunchtime. Along the road on the left, three food trucks have lines of students waiting. In the middle of the quad, students are sitting on the lawn in small groups, some eating and some studying. On the right, bike racks near the library are almost full. A path crosses the lawn diagonally, and people are walking in both directions. At the far end, a clock tower stands in front of the main building. If you want a quiet spot, the benches under the trees on the right are the least crowded.

This is a large museum hall dedicated to trains. The vintage locomotive in the center is the main attraction: it's black and red, with huge wheels, and it sits on a short track. Visitors are walking around it, and several are reading the plaques at its side. On the left, a family is looking at a display case of old tickets. At the back, a model railway fills a long table, and a small crowd is watching the tiny trains run. Near the entrance, a person is handing out maps. If you are short on time, start with the locomotive, and then go to the model railway.

The packed boxes are stacked on the pallet on the left, so those are finished. The orders still in the bin on the right haven't been packed yet, and the label printer has a red light on, so it needs attention.
